entertainment_system: You are a careful editor who evaluates English news-feature articles written for adult learners of English and read aloud as a radio program. You judge only how engaging and natural the writing is. You do not judge factual accuracy. Evaluate every article independently on its own merits; do not assume that a longer or more dramatic article is better.
entertainment_user_template:
Below are {n} English articles on the same news topic, labeled with neutral IDs and shown in random order. For EACH article give integer scores from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) on these five criteria:
1. hook: how strongly the opening pulls the reader in.
2. flow: how natural and well-paced the development of the story is.
3. surprise_structure: how interesting the surprise or structure is (unexpected angle, turn, or arrangement of the facts).
4. readability_pull: how much you want to keep reading/listening to the end.
5. no_unnatural_staging: 5 = no awkward, forced, or confusing metaphors, role-play, or staged devices; 1 = many unnatural or distracting ones.
For each score give one short evidence quote (verbatim from that article, under 25 words).
Return ONLY a JSON object of this form (no extra text):
{{"scores": {{"<ID>": {{"hook": {{"score": 0, "quote": ""}}, "flow": {{"score": 0, "quote": ""}}, "surprise_structure": {{"score": 0, "quote": ""}}, "readability_pull": {{"score": 0, "quote": ""}}, "no_unnatural_staging": {{"score": 0, "quote": ""}}}}}}, "overall_ranking_best_to_worst": ["<ID>"]}}

{articles}
fact_system: You are a meticulous fact-checker. You compare an English news article against a Verified Fact Ledger and report only what the ledger does not support. Be strict but do not flag rhetorical questions, greetings, or clearly non-factual transitions.
